sentences.zh: 他们每个月都在增加更多的订阅者。

sentences.en: And during those years, too, famously, The Washington Post came up with a new motto,
sentences.zh: 在特朗普执政的最初几年里，据称《邮报》是盈利的。

sentences.en: Democracy Dies in Darkness.
sentences.zh: 但随后在拜登政府初期，即21年、22年，它跌落了悬崖，当时数字广告枯竭了，受众也枯竭了。

sentences.en: I remember.
sentences.zh: 从新闻消费者的角度来看，那不是一个那么有趣的时期。

sentences.en: I think those years represented Bezos's promise fulfilled, an era of tremendous success.
sentences.zh: 周六早上，白宫没有每小时都有重大新闻传出。

sentences.en: So during this period of what sounds like a reinvigorated newsroom, how was it doing on the business side?
sentences.zh: 所以新闻少了，危机少了，关注度少了，点击量也少了。

sentences.en: Was it making money?
sentences.zh: 这对《邮报》的业务产生了巨大影响。

sentences.en: Was there a strategy?
sentences.zh: 而且数字广告也出现了下滑。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 所以你得到的结果是，《华盛顿邮报》开始年复一年地亏损，高达1亿美元。

sentences.en: I mean, part of the strategy, of course, was to ride the Trump bump.
sentences.zh: 看着这一切，你有一种阴森的感觉，那就是报纸在数字广告、订阅者方面的系统性问题，这些问题继续困扰着《华盛顿邮报》的账目。

sentences.en: Let's be honest about that.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But they did a lot of things to improve the product.
sentences.zh: 你所说的本质上是，《华盛顿邮报》在特朗普当选后几年里获得的红利，并不是对新战略、新商业模式的反应。

sentences.en: They were bringing on more subscribers month after month.
sentences.zh: 它是对特朗普的反应。

sentences.en: And through those initial Trump years, the Post was allegedly profitable.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普执政的最初几年里，《华盛顿邮报》据称是盈利的。

sentences.en: But then it fell off a cliff sort of in the beginning of the Biden administration, 21, 22, when digital advertising sort of dried up and audience dried up.
sentences.zh: 但到了拜登政府执政初期，也就是21年和22年，情况急转直下，数字广告业务和受众群体都出现了萎缩。

sentences.en: It was not as interesting a time from the viewpoint of a news consumer.
sentences.zh: 从新闻消费者的角度来看，那段时间没那么有吸引力了。

sentences.en: There weren't major stories coming out of the White House hour after hour on a Saturday morning.
sentences.zh: 白宫不再像以前那样，周六早上每隔一小时就爆出重磅新闻。

sentences.en: So that was less news and less crisis and fewer eyeballs, fewer clicks.
sentences.zh: 所以新闻少了，危机少了，关注度也就下降了，点击量也随之减少。

sentences.en: That had a big impact on the Post's business.
sentences.zh: 这对《华盛顿邮报》的业务产生了巨大影响。

sentences.en: And there was also a slump in digital advertising to boot.
sentences.zh: 而且雪上加霜的是，数字广告市场也陷入了低迷。

sentences.en: So what you have then is that the Washington Post started losing a lot of money year after year, up to like $100 million.
sentences.zh: 所以结果就是，《华盛顿邮报》开始连年亏损，金额高达一亿美元左右。

sentences.en: And the eerie sort of feeling you got looking at this is that those systemic problems with
sentences.zh: 看着这些数据，你会产生一种令人不安的感觉，那就是那些系统性问题——

sentences.en: the newspaper relating to digital advertising, subscribers, those problems continue to haunt the Washington Post ledger.
sentences.zh: 报社在数字广告和订阅用户方面的问题，依然在困扰着《华盛顿邮报》的财务报表。

sentences.en: Right.
What you're saying is essentially that the bump that the Washington Post got in the years after Trump was elected was not a response to a new strategy, a new business model.
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，《华盛顿邮报》在特朗普当选后的几年里获得的增长，本质上并非源于新的战略或新的商业模式。

sentences.en: It was a response to Trump.
sentences.zh: 而是对特朗普现象的一种反应。

sentences.en: And so therefore, the Trump bump, this enormous influx of readers right after the election in
sentences.zh: 因此，特朗普效应，也就是大选后读者人数的激增，

sentences.en: 2016, kind of papered over an intractable problem that was much more intractable than perhaps anybody had anticipated.
sentences.zh: 2016年，在某种程度上掩盖了一个比任何人预想中都要棘手得多的难题。

sentences.en: Yes, indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That is essentially what we've learned kind of the hard way, that the Post emerged from these years of profitability.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是我们以惨痛代价学到的教训，即《华盛顿邮报》在经历了这些年的盈利后，情况发生了变化。

sentences.en: And then this went a little bit sideways, that went a little bit sideways.
sentences.zh: 然后事情就有点偏离轨道了，那件事也偏离了轨道。

sentences.en: The audience wasn't fully there, which means that the business model isn't really robuSt.
sentences.zh: 受众并没有完全留住，这意味着商业模式并不稳健。

sentences.en: It can't handle anything less than optimal circumstances.
sentences.zh: 它无法应对任何非最优的情况。

sentences.en: So the Washington Post's business model problems were such that even if you had a management team that was making reasonably smart and logical decisions, the paper would still be
sentences.zh: 所以《华盛顿邮报》的商业模式问题在于，即使你有一个管理团队在做相当明智和合乎逻辑的决策，报纸依然会

sentences.en: struggling.
sentences.zh: 陷入困境。

sentences.en: But starting in 2024, Jeff Bezos took a number of steps that turned a problem into a genuine crisis.
sentences.zh: 但从2024年开始，杰夫·贝索斯采取了一系列措施，将一个问题演变成了一场真正的危机。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·罗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜店打碟的黑胶唱片时代，每天晚上你都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成一个

sentences.en: living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 活生生的、充满50年历史精美文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重塑者》吧。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times Games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题，我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你们刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: So, Eric, before the break, you mentioned that The Post in 2024 hit this state of crisis.
sentences.zh: 那么，埃里克，在休息之前，你提到《华盛顿邮报》在2024年陷入了危机状态。

sentences.en: I think I know what you're talking about, but tell us what happened.
sentences.zh: 我想我知道你在说什么，但请告诉我们发生了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, so what happened in 2024 was really significant.
sentences.zh: 是的，2024年发生的事情确实意义重大。

sentences.en: The election proceeded with respect to our coverage, just as it always had.
sentences.zh: 大选期间，我们的报道工作一如既往地进行。

sentences.en: The news side was doing its articles.
sentences.zh: 新闻部门在撰写文章。

sentences.en: The editorial side was doing its editorials and its op-eds, and things were bumping along just fine.
sentences.zh: 评论部门在撰写社论和专栏文章，一切都进展得很顺利。

sentences.en: Now, as usually happened sometime in late summer, early fall, the Washington Post editorial board would begin drafting and publish an endorsement of one of the candidates in the
sentences.zh: 通常在夏末秋初，华盛顿邮报编辑委员会会开始起草并发布对总统竞选候选人之一的背书，

sentences.en: presidential race.
sentences.zh: 这是惯例。

sentences.en: And this was something that readers had come to expect.
sentences.zh: 读者们对此早已习以为常。

sentences.en: But as we inched closer and closer to the election, there was no editorial coming forth from the Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 但随着大选临近，华盛顿邮报却迟迟没有发布社论。

sentences.en: Nothing was published.
sentences.zh: 什么都没发表。

sentences.en: Nothing was published, even though people on the editorial board were working on one and indeed had mustered a draft endorsement in favor of Democratic candidate Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 什么都没发表，尽管编辑委员会的人正在撰写，甚至已经起草了一份支持民主党候选人卡玛拉·哈里斯的背书草案。

sentences.en: But 11 days before the election, Will Lewis, the publisher, announced that there would be a new policy.
sentences.zh: 但在大选前11天，出版人威尔·刘易斯宣布了一项新政策。

sentences.en: And that policy was to not publish endorsements at all in this race and in future races.
sentences.zh: 该政策规定，在本次及未来的竞选中不再发布任何背书。

sentences.en: It was articulated as a policy shift and not as some sort of political decision.
sentences.zh: 这被解释为政策调整，而非某种政治决策。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Explain the reaction to that a little bit.
sentences.zh: 解释一下对此的反应吧。

sentences.en: It was epic.
sentences.zh: 反响非常强烈。

sentences.en: People went berserk on the Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 人们对《华盛顿邮报》感到愤怒。

sentences.en: You mean people were writing in and expressing their displeasure.
sentences.zh: 你是说人们写信表达了他们的不满。

sentences.en: Our digital messaging platforms were aflame.
sentences.zh: 我们的数字消息平台都炸锅了。

sentences.en: They were very busy.
sentences.zh: 它们非常繁忙。

sentences.en: And people answered immediately with their money and they canceled their subscriptions.
sentences.zh: 人们立即用金钱做出了回应，他们取消了订阅。

sentences.en: NPR reported that there were in excess of 250,000 cancellations of subscriptions against a subscriber base that was about 2.5 million at the time.
sentences.zh: 据NPR报道，当时订阅用户基数约为250万，而取消订阅的人数超过了25万。

sentences.en: And Eric, why did people have that kind of reaction, given the fact that an owner of a newspaper traditionally has the right to influence the editorial page?
sentences.zh: 埃里克，考虑到报纸所有者传统上拥有影响社论版面的权利，为什么人们会有那样的反应？

sentences.en: Yes, that's traditionally the prerogative of owners.
sentences.zh: 是的，这在传统上是所有者的特权。

sentences.en: And it's been cemented for decades in American newspapering.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，这在美国报业中已根深蒂固。

sentences.en: But what was particularly problematic here was not necessarily that Bezos had instituted a new policy, per se.
sentences.zh: 但这里特别成问题的不一定是贝索斯制定了新政策本身。

sentences.en: The issue was when it happened and what had preceded it.
sentences.zh: 问题在于它发生的时间以及之前的铺垫。

sentences.en: When it happened was 11 days before the election.
sentences.zh: 它发生在大选前11天。

sentences.en: And what preceded it was that the Washington Post had a draft endorsement for Kamala Harris in the hopper, ready to go.
sentences.zh: 而在此之前，《华盛顿邮报》已经准备好了一份支持卡玛拉·哈里斯的背书草案。

sentences.en: So many people just did the shorthand and say, Jeff Bezos killed the Kamala Harris editorial.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人直接得出结论：杰夫·贝索斯扼杀了卡玛拉·哈里斯的社论。

sentences.en: Now, the Washington Post's statement was written to kind of prevent that impression from taking hold.
sentences.zh: 《华盛顿邮报》的声明旨在防止这种印象扎根。

sentences.en: But it wasn't very effective in doing that.
sentences.zh: 但效果并不理想。

sentences.en: And a not insignificant portion of subscribers canceled, it seemed, because of this decision to pull the endorsement.
sentences.zh: 看起来，相当一部分订阅者正是因为撤回背书的决定而取消了订阅。

sentences.en: There was no uncertainty about the cause and effect here.
sentences.zh: 对于因果关系，没有任何不确定性。

sentences.en: None.
sentences.zh: 一点也没有。

sentences.en: This drop happened because of this decision.
sentences.zh: 这次流失就是因为这个决定。

sentences.en: And people at the Post were livid about it.
sentences.zh: 邮报的员工对此感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And they were also insistent.
sentences.zh: 他们也坚持认为：

sentences.en: We should not be held liable for this particular loss.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该为这次特定的损失承担责任。

sentences.en: This one's on management.
sentences.zh: 这是管理层的错。

sentences.en: They should take the consequences of this awful decision and not foist it on us via cutbacks, layoffs, buyouts, whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们应该承担这个糟糕决定的后果，而不是通过削减开支、裁员、买断等方式强加给我们。

sentences.en: I remember this moment as really the first clearest example of something happening that
sentences.zh: 我记得那一刻是人们担心贝索斯收购报纸后会发生的事情的第一个最清晰的例子，

sentences.en: people had worried would happen when Bezos bought the paper, which is that he would make a decision that at least seemed like it was caving to power.
sentences.zh: 那就是他会做出一个看起来像是向权力低头的决定。

sentences.en: In this case, giving what seemed like a gift to then-candidate Trump.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，就像是给当时的候选人特朗普送了一份大礼。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, you have a lot of company in reaching that conclusion, is all I would say there.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我只能说，得出这个结论的人不在少数。

sentences.en: And of course, that wasn't the end of it.
sentences.zh: 当然，事情还没完。

sentences.en: Just months later, in February of 2025, Bezos, just out of nowhere, declared a pivot in the
sentences.zh: 仅仅几个月后，在2025年2月，贝索斯毫无征兆地宣布《华盛顿邮报》评论版块的意识形态转向个人自由和自由市场。

sentences.en: Washington Post opinion section's ideological outlook towards personal liberties and free markets.
sentences.zh: 这突如其来，人们再次得出结论，这是一种为了迎合唐纳德·特朗普和共和党而调整评论方向的方式。

sentences.en: And that came out of the blue, and again, people reached the conclusion that this was a way of pivoting the opinion offerings in favor of Donald Trump and the GOP.
sentences.zh: 然后我想说，在接下来的几个月里，这种失望情绪加深了。

sentences.en: And then I would say that there was a dismay that deepened over the course of several months.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对领导层的日益不满开始显现，许多人选择了接受买断离职。

sentences.en: I think that there started to be a growing dissatisfaction with leadership, and a number of people took a buyout to leave.
sentences.zh: 其他人则直接选择离开。

sentences.en: Other people just chose to leave.
sentences.zh: 包括你，对吧？

sentences.en: Including you, right?
sentences.zh: 包括我。

sentences.en: Including me.
sentences.zh: 是我妻子给了我一巴掌，说‘醒醒吧，伙计’，因为我当时对一切的发展方向处于一种否认状态。

sentences.en: That was my wife who slapped me and said, wake up, bucko, pretty much, because I was sort of in a state of denial about where everything was headed.
sentences.zh: 我想我们很多人都有同样的感觉，我们在这样一个机构待了这么久，它一直如此稳定、如此可靠，以至于我们无法相信

sentences.en: I think a lot of us had that same sort of feeling that we had been at this institution for so long, it had been so steady, it had been so reliable, that we could not believe that
sentences.zh: 脚下的土地正在发生动摇。

sentences.en: the ground was shifting underneath our feet.
sentences.zh: 但那里确实存在一种情绪，认为事情管理得并不好，考虑得也不够周全。

sentences.en: But there is and was a sentiment there that things were just not very well managed and very well thought through.
sentences.zh: 这在以前从未发生过。

sentences.en: And that had never been the case before.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是导致大量离职和不满情绪的因素。

sentences.en: And that was, I think, the factor that drove a lot of departures and drove a lot of dissatisfaction.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，我们所谈论的一切并非发生在真空中。

sentences.en: It feels worth noting that none of what we are talking about is happening in a vacuum.
sentences.zh: 特别是本周发生的裁员。

sentences.en: The layoffs in particular that have happened this week.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·贝索斯刚刚向第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普控制的一家公司支付了7500万美元用于拍摄一部纪录片。

sentences.en: Jeff Bezos just paid $75 million to a company controlled by Melania Trump, the first lady, for a documentary.
sentences.zh: 这是一笔巨额资金。

sentences.en: It's an exorbitant amount of money.
sentences.zh: 这导致很多人说，这简直就是赤裸裸地试图讨好政府。

sentences.en: It's caused a lot of people to say that this is nothing short of a transparent attempt to cozy up to the administration.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊也是总统所推行的东翼宴会厅项目的主要捐助者之一。

sentences.en: Amazon is also one of the top donors to the East Wing Ballroom Project the president has pursued.
sentences.zh: 而这一切都发生在一个对新闻界进行前所未有的攻击的时期，包括在《华盛顿邮报》，

sentences.en: And all of this is happening at a time of unprecedented attacks on the press, including at the Washington
sentences.zh: 那里的一位记者最近家被FBI搜查了。

sentences.en: Post, where a journalist recently had her home searched by the FBI.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为很多人可能在听这个节目，听到了所有这些背景，

sentences.en: And so I think a lot of people are probably listening to this and have heard all of this context
sentences.zh: 并思考着世界上和新闻界正在发生的其他所有事情。

sentences.en: and are thinking about all the other things going on right now in the world and in the world of journalism.
sentences.zh: 他们想知道，我们谈论的这些裁员是否以某种方式符合这一背景？

sentences.en: And they're wondering, do these cuts that we are talking about fit into that backdrop in any way?
sentences.zh: 我会说，如果你打算以任何方式削减新闻编辑室来取悦唐纳德·特朗普，我认为这些裁员方式会不同。

sentences.en: I am going to say if you are going to cut a newsroom to please Donald Trump in any way, I think that those cuts would have been different.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们会首先针对《华盛顿邮报》的调查能力、政治版块和国家安全版块。

sentences.en: In other words, they would have gone first after the investigative capacity, the politics desk, the national security desk of The Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 这些版块多年来对特朗普总统造成的损害最大。

sentences.en: Those desks have done the greatest damage over the years to President Trump.
sentences.zh: 而你刚才列出的那些版块，明确地说，它们保持完整。

sentences.en: And the desks that you just outlined, to be clear, those are remaining intact.
sentences.zh: 好吧，它们比那些被针对的版块保持得更完整。

sentences.en: Well, those are remaining more intact than the ones that they targeted.
sentences.zh: 管理层表示，裁员几乎影响了新闻编辑室的所有领域，但受影响最直接、比例最深的是大都会版块、体育版块和国际版块。

sentences.en: Management has said that the cuts affect pretty much all areas of the newsroom, but the most
sentences.zh: 所以我认为那种解读在这里并不适用。

sentences.en: directly affected, the most proportionately deep cuts fell on the Metro sports and the international staffs.
sentences.zh: 我认为更广泛的批评是，贝索斯正在掏空他曾经支持、投资并扩张的新闻编辑室。

sentences.en: So I don't think that that particular read is operative here.
sentences.zh: 所以我们基本上看到的是他对新闻编辑室投资的收回。

sentences.en: The broader critique at play, I think, is just that Bezos is gutting the newsroom that he once propped up and that he once invested in and that he expanded.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就像一个回旋镖。

sentences.en: So we're basically seeing a clawback of the investment that he put into the newsroom.
sentences.zh: 所以这对《华盛顿邮报》来说是一场灾难。

sentences.en: It's basically like a boomerang.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重大的媒体新闻。

sentences.en: So that is kind of a cataclysm at The Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 为什么要加倍投入你提到的那些版块？

sentences.en: That is a major, major media story.
sentences.zh: 国家安全、政治、调查。

sentences.en: Why double down on the desks that you mentioned?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些版块是他和其他领导层押注的对象？

sentences.en: National security, politics, investigations.
sentences.zh: 嗯，解释是他们通过查看数据、查看分析，发现了读者想要的领域。

sentences.en: Why are those desks the ones that he and the rest of the leadership are banking on?
sentences.zh: 他们降低了读者不想要的那些版块的权重。

sentences.en: Well, the explanation is that they have found, through looking at the data, through looking at the analytics, the areas that readers want.
sentences.zh: 我们没有他们所有的分析数据。

sentences.en: And they've de-emphasized the ones that readers don't want.
sentences.zh: 但这就是理由，他们查看了分析数据。

sentences.en: We don't have all their analytics.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是前进的方向，也是拯救该机构的途径。

sentences.en: But that's the rationale, that they looked at the analytics.
sentences.zh: 不过是通过缩小机构规模来拯救。

sentences.en: They decided that this was the way to go and that this was the route to saving the institution.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Saving by shrinking the institution, though.
sentences.zh: 我可以理解为什么加倍投入你认为的核心产品是有道理的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 但我读一段杰夫·贝索斯收购报纸时说的话。

sentences.en: I can understand why that might make sense to double down on what you believe to be your core product.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你可以一直缩小业务规模。

sentences.en: But I want to read you something that Jeff Bezos said when he bought the paper.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过缩小规模来盈利，这是一种生存策略。

sentences.en: I don't think you can keep shrinking the business.
sentences.zh: 但它最终会导致无关紧要。

sentences.en: You can be profitable and shrinking, and that's a survival strategy.
sentences.zh: 最坏的情况是，它会导致灭绝。

sentences.en: But it ultimately leads to irrelevance at beSt.
sentences.zh: 那么，如果这与加倍投入那几个核心领域的想法有任何关联的话，它是如何协调的呢？

sentences.en: And at worst, it leads to extinction.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我确实认为其中有一些逻辑，那就是《邮报》在这些领域表现出色。

sentences.en: So how does that square, if it squares at all, with the idea of doubling down on just those few core areas?
sentences.zh: 问题是他们正在削减人们过去喜欢的所有内容。

sentences.en: Well, I do think that there is some logic there, and that is that the Post has had a tremendous run in these areas.
sentences.zh: 每当报纸削减内容时，就会出现流失。

sentences.en: The problem is that they are cutting all kinds of stuff that people have enjoyed in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 这种流失基本上降低了他们的收入。

sentences.en: And whenever a newspaper cuts, there is a desertion.
sentences.zh: 它削减了他们的收入，因为订阅者离开了，数字广告商看不到他们想要投放广告的内容。

sentences.en: And that desertion basically lowers their revenue.
sentences.zh: 所以你进入了一种螺旋，业内人士称之为死亡螺旋，即你削减产品，人们离开报纸，收入下降。

sentences.en: It cuts into their revenue because subscribers leave, digital advertisers don't see as much content they want to be adjacent to.
sentences.zh: 你削减更多，人们离开，你再削减更多。

sentences.en: And so you get into sort of a spiral, which people in the industry call a death spiral, where you cut the product, people desert the paper, revenues go down.
sentences.zh: 这是一个自我强化的循环。

sentences.en: You cut more, people desert, you cut more.
sentences.zh: 这是一种痛苦。

sentences.en: And it's a self-reinforcing cycle.
sentences.zh: 而且没有任何保证表明《邮报》不会陷入这些螺旋之一。

sentences.en: And it's misery.
sentences.zh: 因为加倍投入这些领域是否能支撑商业模式是一个悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: And there is no guarantee whatsoever that the Post is not descending into one of those spirals.
sentences.zh: 根本没有保证它会成功。

sentences.en: Because there is an open question as to whether doubling down on these areas is going to float the business model.
sentences.zh: 埃里克，我想再读一段话。

sentences.en: There is just no guarantee that it will.
sentences.zh: 这是马蒂·巴伦周三声明中的一段引语。

sentences.en: I want to read you one more thing, Eric.
sentences.zh: 马蒂·巴伦，《华盛顿邮报》前执行主编。

sentences.en: And this is a quote from Marty Barron's statement on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 他的声明说，

sentences.en: Marty Barron, former executive editor of The Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 审视你列出的所有裁员，审视《邮报》内外人们的反应，正如我提到的，用末日般的措辞来谈论这件事，你认为我们能对《邮报》进行我们所期待和依赖的那种新闻报道的能力说些什么？

sentences.en: And his statement says,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我会说我们永远不应该低估那里记者的能力。

sentences.en: Looking at all the cuts that you've outlined, looking at the reaction from people both inside
sentences.zh: 审视你列出的所有裁员，审视《邮报》内外人们的反应，正如我提到的，用末日般的措辞来谈论这件事，你认为我们能对《邮报》进行我们所期待和依赖的那种新闻报道的能力说些什么？

sentences.en: and outside the Post, talking about this in, as I mentioned, apocalyptic terms, what do you think we can say about the Post's ability to do the kind of journalism we have come to
sentences.zh: 审视你列出的所有裁员，审视《邮报》内外人们的反应，正如我提到的，用末日般的措辞来谈论这件事，你认为我们能对《邮报》进行我们所期待和依赖的那种新闻报道的能力说些什么？

sentences.en: expect and rely on from this paper?
sentences.zh: 审视你列出的所有裁员，审视《邮报》内外人们的反应，正如我提到的，用末日般的措辞来谈论这件事，你认为我们能对《邮报》进行我们所期待和依赖的那种新闻报道的能力说些什么？

sentences.en: Well, I would say we should never sell short the abilities of the journalists that are there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我会说我们永远不应该低估那里记者的能力。

sentences.en: When a story emerges, they will get on it.
sentences.zh: 一旦有新闻出现，他们就会跟进。

sentences.en: And they will continue investigating.
sentences.zh: 他们会继续调查。

sentences.en: They will continue breaking news.
sentences.zh: 他们会继续发布新闻。

sentences.en: They will continue kicking ass in journalism.
sentences.zh: 他们会在新闻界继续大显身手。

sentences.en: So people will continue.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会继续支持。

sentences.en: I will continue to subscribe to The Washington Post as I have for decades.
sentences.zh: 我会像过去几十年一样，继续订阅《华盛顿邮报》。

sentences.en: Nothing will make me ever stop my subscription to The Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 没有什么能让我停止订阅《华盛顿邮报》。

sentences.en: I get it in print.
sentences.zh: 我订阅的是纸质版。

sentences.en: I read it every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都读。

sentences.en: I've read it through this tumult, too.
sentences.zh: 即使在动荡时期，我也一直在读。

sentences.en: Every day I find plenty to read in The Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 每天我都能在《华盛顿邮报》里找到大量值得阅读的内容。

sentences.en: It will not stop producing really good journalism.
sentences.zh: 它不会停止产出高质量的新闻报道。

sentences.en: What will happen is we will never see the stuff that they just don't have the manpower to produce.
sentences.zh: 将会发生的是，我们永远也看不到那些他们因人手不足而无法报道的内容。

sentences.en: So this becomes something that is utterly ineffable, utterly invisible, and utterly impossible to quantify.
sentences.zh: 所以这变成了一件完全无法言说、完全隐形且完全无法量化的事情。

sentences.en: That there will be things going on in the world that The Washington Post does not have the resources or the eyes to see through.
sentences.zh: 世界上将会有一些事情发生，而《华盛顿邮报》却没有资源或眼力去洞察。

sentences.en: Eric Wumpel, thank you so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 埃里克·温佩尔，非常感谢您加入我们的节目。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是您今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: We currently have an unprecedented number of counties communicating with us now
sentences.zh: 目前有数量空前的县正在与我们沟通，

sentences.en: and allowing ICE to take custody of illegal aliens before they hit the streets.
sentences.zh: 并允许移民及海关执法局（ICE）在非法移民流落街头前将其拘留。

sentences.en: Unprecedented cooperation.
sentences.zh: 史无前例的合作。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the president's border czar Tom Homan said that the government would immediately withdraw 700 officers from Minneapolis
sentences.zh: 周三，总统的边境事务主管汤姆·霍曼表示，政府将立即从明尼阿波利斯撤出700名官员，

sentences.en: after local officials agreed to increase their cooperation with federal immigration agents.
sentences.zh: 此前当地官员同意加强与联邦移民局特工的合作。

sentences.en: The cooperation, Homan said, involves local officials allowing ICE agents to take custody of undocumented immigrants before they are released from jail.
sentences.zh: 霍曼说，这种合作包括当地官员允许ICE特工在无证移民从监狱获释前将其拘留。

sentences.en: More officers taking custody of criminal aliens directly from the jails means less officers on the street doing criminal operations.
sentences.zh: 更多的官员直接从监狱接管犯罪外籍人员，意味着在街头执行刑事行动的官员会减少。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court has cleared the way for California to use a new congressional map explicitly designed to help Democrats in this fall's midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 最高法院已为加利福尼亚州扫清障碍，允许其使用一张旨在帮助民主党人在今年秋季中期选举中获胜的国会选区图。

sentences.en: The justices rejected an emergency request by the California Republican Party to block the map.
sentences.zh: 大法官们驳回了加州共和党提出的阻止该地图的紧急请求。

sentences.en: Democrats redrew the state's congressional districts last year to counter a similar effort undertaken by Republicans at President Trump's behest in states like Texas.
sentences.zh: 民主党人去年重新划分了该州的国会选区，以反击特朗普总统在德克萨斯州等地授意共和党人采取的类似举措。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Carlos Prieto, Shannon Lynn, and Eric Krupke.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由卡洛斯·普列托、香农·林恩和埃里克·克鲁普克制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Devin Taylor and Lizzo Balin.
sentences.zh: 由德文·泰勒和利佐·巴林编辑。

sentences.en: Contains music by Dan Powell, Sophia Landman, Diane Wong, and Rowan Nemisto.
sentences.zh: 包含丹·鲍威尔、索菲亚·兰德曼、黛安·王和罗文·内米斯托的音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德负责工程制作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我，萨拉·凯尼格，将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何平台收听。
